beats.narration_slice: In 1901, divers found a wreck near Antikythera.
beats.visual: Vertical layered paper-cut underwater scene: two period divers descend toward a broken ancient ship resting on a rocky Mediterranean seabed, with amphorae and timber fragments emerging from cool slate-blue water.
beats.purpose: show the 1901 discovery of the Antikythera shipwreck
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide underwater establishing shot + two descending divers + wreck and amphorae on rocky seabed + cool slate-blue depth with amber surface light + diagonal top-to-bottom composition
beats.continuity: begin the subject world underwater at the wreck site, fully separate from the opening environment

beats.narration_slice: A corroded lump hid bronze gears.
beats.visual: Close paper-cut archaeological reveal of a diver's gloved hands lifting an irregular green-brown corroded bronze mass, with one small honey-amber gear edge visible through a cracked encrusted surface.
beats.purpose: show that an unremarkable corroded fragment concealed geared machinery
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme close-up + encrusted bronze lump in gloved hands + tiny exposed gear teeth + dark wreck shadow behind + centered discovery composition
beats.continuity: move from the wreck overview to one recovered object from the same seabed

beats.narration_slice: The mechanism was about two millennia old.
beats.visual: Paper-cut time metaphor showing the corroded mechanism fragment in the foreground while a ghosted Hellenistic Greek ship and ancient coastal silhouette appear far behind it in warm cream and muted olive layers.
beats.purpose: establish that the mechanism dates back roughly two thousand years
beats.visual_fingerprint: foreground artifact silhouette + distant ancient Greek ship and coast + compressed side profile composition + warm amber historical glow replacing underwater blue
beats.continuity: shift from physical discovery to the artifact's ancient historical origin

beats.narration_slice: A hand crank turned interlocking wheels.
beats.visual: Cutaway paper reconstruction of the mechanism viewed three-quarter close, with a simple side crank being turned by the Red Horned Everyman and several bronze gear wheels visibly meshing inside the case.
beats.purpose: show how manual cranking drove the interlocking gear train
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-quarter mechanical cutaway + host hand on side crank + layered meshing bronze wheels + cream workshop-like void + strong left-to-right mechanical flow
beats.continuity: move from age and origin into a reconstructed explanation of how the mechanism operated

beats.narration_slice: Pointers tracked the Sun and Moon.
beats.visual: Front-facing paper-cut dial with two distinct pointer arms sweeping across a circular celestial face, one ending in a restrained amber Sun disc and the other in a pale cream Moon disc.
beats.purpose: show that front pointers represented the positions of the Sun and Moon
beats.visual_fingerprint: straight-on circular dial + paired Sun and Moon pointer arms + no host + symmetrical centered composition + cream face with olive and amber celestial accents
beats.continuity: follow the crank's mechanical motion to what the gearing displayed on the front

beats.narration_slice: Other gears displayed the Moon’s changing phase.
beats.visual: Paper-cut close-up of a small two-tone lunar sphere mounted on the mechanism, half cream and half slate, with compact bronze gears beneath indicating the sphere's rotation from bright to dark.
beats.purpose: explain the geared display of lunar phases
beats.visual_fingerprint: macro detail + half-light half-dark Moon sphere + compact gear pair beneath + shallow layered backdrop + off-center upper-right composition
beats.continuity: stay with astronomical outputs but isolate the Moon-phase mechanism from the larger pointer dial

beats.visual: Rear view of the reconstructed mechanism in paper cut, dominated by broad nested circular and spiral tracks with a slender indicator arm moving through repeated calendar divisions, all without readable markings.
beats.purpose: show that the back of the mechanism tracked repeating calendar cycles
beats.visual_fingerprint: rear elevation + large nested dial tracks + single indicator arm + mechanism casing edges framing both sides + muted olive background with honey-bronze rings
beats.continuity: rotate conceptually from front astronomical displays to the mechanism's rear dial system

beats.visual: Tight paper-cut view of one rear spiral dial, with its pointer advancing along the spiral while a stylized dark Moon overlaps an amber Sun above the dial as an eclipse symbol.
beats.purpose: show that one spiral cycle was used to forecast eclipses
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight spiral-dial crop + advancing pointer + overlapping Sun and dark Moon symbol + diagonal lower-left to upper-right composition + dramatic amber-to-slate contrast
beats.continuity: zoom from the general rear calendar system into one specific predictive spiral

beats.narration_slice: Another marked major games, including the Olympics.
beats.visual: Paper-cut dial segment beside a symbolic ancient athletic scene: a small laurel wreath, stadium curve, and two simplified Greek runners appear as visual motifs linked to a pointer on the mechanism, with no lettering.
beats.purpose: show that a separate cycle indicated major Panhellenic games such as the Olympics
beats.visual_fingerprint: mechanism dial on left + laurel wreath and two runners on right + warm sunlit stadium motif + split but unified storybook composition + no eclipse or lunar imagery
beats.continuity: move from astronomical prediction to a different rear-dial function tied to civic games

beats.visual: The Red Horned Everyman stands beside a tabletop exploded reconstruction made of layered paper bronze gears suspended in depth, calmly studying how separated wheels align into one dense mechanism.
beats.purpose: show modern reconstruction of the gear arrangement hidden inside the damaged artifact
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium three-quarter host view + exploded gear assembly hovering over table + multiple depth layers + warm cream archaeological study setting + host gaze guiding inward
beats.continuity: leave the ancient dial functions and show how researchers inferred the internal machinery

beats.narration_slice: Its complexity inspired the nickname ancient computer.
beats.visual: Dense paper-cut reconstruction fills the frame like an intricate mechanical brain, dozens of interlocking bronze wheels nested inside the case while the outer silhouette remains unmistakably ancient and non-electronic.
beats.purpose: communicate why the mechanism's extraordinary mechanical complexity earned the ancient computer nickname
beats.visual_fingerprint: front-on dense gear lattice + mechanism shaped as compact mechanical brain metaphor + no host + dark olive vignette around bright honey gear core + vertically centered complexity focus
beats.continuity: compress the reconstructed gearwork into one striking image emphasizing its unusual sophistication

beats.narration_slice: It modeled the sky without electricity.
beats.visual: Final paper-cut tableau of the complete bronze mechanism below a layered celestial arc of Sun, Moon, stars, and orbital curves, with the Red Horned Everyman quietly observing from the lower edge and no wires, batteries, or modern components.
beats.purpose: show that purely mechanical gearing represented celestial cycles without electrical power
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle final tableau + complete mechanism beneath sweeping celestial arc + small observing host at lower edge + warm amber sky against slate-blue outer layers + expansive upward composition
beats.continuity: resolve the reconstruction sequence by connecting the physical gears directly to the sky they modeled
